deck: Selected work in agent infrastructure, commerce systems, and developer tooling.
origin: I read architecture and sculpture before I wrote software, and both are trainings in deciding where a thing ends — which is most of what the work above is.

caseStudies.name: Bounded Systems
caseStudies.problem: Agent-authored commits reached main without review, and afterwards nobody could say which writes the agent had been authorized to make.
caseStudies.intervention: Moved privileged git effects behind capability-checked operations, and routed the work through one pipeline whose only exit is a merged pull request.
caseStudies.evidence: prx drives a work unit to an attributed pull request; ocap-provenance records which capabilities each effect held, and which were denied. Both are public, and both name what is still outside the check.
caseStudies.role: System model, schemas, implementation, and the operational testing.

caseStudies.name: Commerce systems
caseStudies.problem: A 9-tab spreadsheet was the supply plan of record, and three teams each read it differently.
caseStudies.intervention: Replaced it with a CLI over one source of truth — 61 schema contracts, 173 test scenarios — and automated the inbound freight it had been gating.
caseStudies.evidence: The three teams now plan against the same document, and freight moves without the manual coordination that used to hold shipments.
caseStudies.role: Contract design, the CLI, and the cross-team consolidation.

caseStudies.name: Developer systems
caseStudies.problem: Whole classes of defect were being found after merge, by people, one ticket at a time.
caseStudies.intervention: Moved static analysis into the pull-request pipeline as a blocking gate, so those classes could not reach main in the first place.
caseStudies.evidence: Critical bugs fell 20% — critical-severity tickets per quarter, the four quarters before against the four after.
caseStudies.role: Gate design, the CI implementation, and the developer-experience work that kept the gate from being routed around.
